Circumcision of the Heart
sur-kum-SIZH-un uv thuh HART
noun phrase
From the Hebrew mul (to circumcise) applied figuratively to the heart; the inward cutting away of sin that the outward sign foreshadowed.

See also: Circumcision of the Heart · Circumcision of the Heart · Circumcision of the Heart

📖 Biblical Definition

Circumcision of the heart is the inward, spiritual work of regeneration whereby God cuts away the corruption and hardness of the soul, fulfilling what the outward sign in the flesh could only foreshadow. Moses promised that the LORD would circumcise the heart of His people to love Him with all the heart and soul, that they might live. Paul declares that he is not a Jew who is one outwardly, neither is that circumcision which is outward in the flesh; but circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit and not in the letter, whose praise is not of men but of God. Thus the true seed of Abraham are those whose hearts God has renewed, not merely those who bear the badge in the body. In Colossians the apostle joins this circumcision made without hands to union with Christ, the putting off of the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ, accomplished in regeneration and signified in baptism. This work is monergistic: God alone wields the knife, for the natural man cannot soften his own stony heart. It is the removal of the foreskin of unbelief, the implanting of a new principle of life and love, and the making of a willing people who delight in the law of God after the inward man. Here the shadow gives way to substance: the sign in the flesh pointed all along to this saving renewal of the heart by the Spirit of God.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The inward work of regeneration that cuts away sin's corruption, fulfilling what outward circumcision foreshadowed.

CIRCUMCISION OF THE HEART, noun phrase. From the Hebrew mul, to circumcise, applied figuratively to the renewing of the inner man.

The inward spiritual renewal of regeneration, of which fleshly circumcision was the outward sign.

A work wrought by God alone, who cuts away the hardness and corruption of the heart.

Moses foretells in Deuteronomy 30:6 that "the LORD thy God will circumcise thine heart, and the heart of thy seed, to love the LORD thy God with all thine heart."

Paul teaches that true circumcision is "that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter."

📖 Key Scripture

Deu 30:6 — "And the LORD thy God will circumcise thine heart, and the heart of thy seed, to love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, that thou mayest live."

Rom 2:29 — "But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God."

Col 2:11 — "In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ:"

Jer 4:4 — "Circumcise yourselves to the LORD, and take away the foreskins of your heart, ye men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem:"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Men trust the outward badge or rite while the heart remains uncircumcised and unrenewed.

expand to see more

The perennial error is to rest in the outward sign while the inward reality is wholly lacking. Israel boasted in circumcised flesh while their hearts remained hard and rebellious; so men today may trust in baptism, church membership, or religious heritage while the soul has never been renewed by the Spirit. The sign without the substance saves no one, for God looks upon the heart and is not deceived by the badge in the body.

To recover the truth we must press home that God requires a circumcised heart, and that He alone can give it. The outward sign was never meant to stand alone but to point to the inward cutting away of sin that comes by regeneration. Therefore men must not rest in any rite but cry to God for the new heart He has promised, knowing that true religion is inward, spiritual, and wrought by the Spirit of the living God.

The inward circumcision is the reality long foreshadowed by the outward sign in the flesh.

Colossians joins this circumcision without hands to union with Christ in regeneration.

The work is monergistic: God alone cuts away the hardness of the soul.

Usage

"The preacher warns hearers not to rest in the outward sign while the heart remains unrenewed."

"Believers thank God for the circumcision made without hands wrought in their regeneration."
